common_name: Evangeline Sweet Potato (LSU Crack-Resistant Orange Gulf Coast Sweet Potato)

planting.note: Plant slips in warm soil after last frost when soil reaches 65F; Evangeline was bred at the LSU AgCenter as an earlier-maturing, crack-resistant alternative to Beauregard and performs especially well in Louisiana's heavy, sometimes wet clay soils where standard varieties are prone to splitting.

directions: Plant rooted slips in well-drained, sandy-loam soil in full sun after last frost; Evangeline is an LSU AgCenter release named for the Cajun heroine of Longfellow's poem and bred to match Beauregard's rich orange flesh and copper skin while ripening slightly earlier and resisting the growth cracking that Beauregard develops in wet Louisiana clay. Vines are moderately compact, and roots are uniform, smooth-skinned, and store well. Flavor is sweet and moist, excellent baked, mashed, or roasted. Because it matures a week or two earlier than Beauregard, Evangeline is a good choice for gardeners wanting an earlier harvest window or extra insurance against fall frost. Cure roots at 80-85F and high humidity for about a week after digging to heal skins and concentrate sugars, then store in a cool, dark, well-ventilated spot.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Evangeline sweet potato release notes
Mississippi State University Extension — Sweet Potato Variety Trials

common_name: Gulfking Peach (Texas A&M Low-Chill Gulf Coast Freestone Peach)

planting.note: Plant bare-root trees in January-February while dormant; Gulfking requires only about 400 chill hours, part of the Texas A&M 'Gulf' series bred for zone 8b-9 coastal Texas and Louisiana where winters are too mild for standard peach varieties. Self-fertile, no pollinizer required.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic loam in full sun; Gulfking is a freestone peach developed by Texas A&M AgriLife as part of its low-chill 'Gulf' series (alongside Gulfprince and Gulfcrest) bred specifically for the mild-winter Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coast. With a chill requirement of roughly 400 hours, it sets a reliable crop in zone 8b-9 areas where standard peach varieties bloom erratically or fail from insufficient winter chilling. Fruit is medium-large, yellow-fleshed, and fully freestone with good classic peach flavor, ripening in late May to early June. Trees are vigorous and self-fertile. Thin fruit to 6-8 inches apart in April to size the crop properly, and prune to an open-center vase shape after leaf drop to maintain good light penetration and airflow in humid Gulf Coast conditions.
sources: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Peach Variety Selection for Texas and the Gulf Coast
LSU AgCenter — Low-Chill Peach Variety Recommendations for the Gulf South
Texas A&M University Stone Fruit Breeding Program — Gulf series release notes

common_name: Gulfprince Peach (Texas A&M Low-Chill Gulf Coast Freestone Peach)

planting.note: Plant bare-root trees in January-February while dormant; Gulfprince requires roughly 400 chill hours and ripens earlier than Gulfking, part of the Texas A&M 'Gulf' series bred for zone 8b-9 coastal Texas and Louisiana. Self-fertile, no pollinizer required.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic loam in full sun; Gulfprince is a freestone peach from the Texas A&M AgriLife low-chill 'Gulf' series, bred alongside Gulfking and Gulfcrest for the mild-winter Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coast where standard peach varieties fail to accumulate enough winter chilling. It requires about 400 chill hours and ripens slightly earlier than Gulfking, giving Gulf Coast growers a way to extend the harvest window when the two are planted together. Fruit is medium-sized, yellow-fleshed, and freestone with good flavor for a low-chill selection, ripening in mid-to-late May. Trees are vigorous and self-fertile. Thin fruit to 6-8 inches apart in April, and prune to an open-center vase shape after leaf drop to maintain airflow and reduce brown rot pressure in humid conditions.
sources: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Peach Variety Selection for Texas and the Gulf Coast
LSU AgCenter — Low-Chill Peach Variety Recommendations for the Gulf South
Texas A&M University Stone Fruit Breeding Program — Gulf series release notes
